summary.oneLiner: Bata delivered a second consecutive quarter of accelerating, volume-backed ~5%+ value growth with broad-based gains across channels and categories, while a structural turnaround (zero-based merchandising at 700 stores, inventory down 28% over two years, franchise/SIS expansion, the 2,000-store EBO milestone) is finally translating into ~11% like-for-like PBT growth and +18% operating cash flow. Reported PBT collapsed ~94% purely on non-recurring/non-cash items (a manufacturing-plant closure/VRS charge, a ~INR22 cr Ind-AS FX revaluation of the brand-licensing liability, and lower lease-closure gains), and the multi-year revenue stagnation is being attacked through product reinvention (only ~10% of which has reached consumers), a forthcoming sneaker proposition for younger buyers, and a stabilising sub-INR1,000 value segment.
summary.business: Bata India Limited operates as a single-segment footwear and accessories company, serving men, women, and kids through a wide range of brands including Bata, Hush Puppies, Power, and Floatz. The company reaches customers via its extensive network of company-owned and franchise stores, multi-brand outlets, key accounts, and a growing digital multi-channel business comprising its own website, mobile app, and marketplaces. It also serves institutional and industrial clients through its non-retail division and acts as a regional design and sourcing hub for the Bata Group.

endMarkets: India (Tier 1 to Tier 5 cities)|Global exports (as a sourcing hub for Bata Group)

financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4/FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (value growth) | ~5%+ | 2nd consecutive accel. quarter | Volume-backed, broad-based across channels & categories |
| Reported PBT | — | **-94%** | Headline distorted by 4 exceptional/non-cash items (see below) |
| Like-to-like PBT (ex one-offs) | — | **+11%** | Mgmt's "clean" number; pre-Ind-AS profit growth ~16% |
| Cash flow from operations | — | **+18%** | Validates the underlying operating leverage |
| Gross margin | Optically flat/diluted | — | Channel mix (franchise lower GM% but EBIT-accretive) + base effect of a ~INR6 cr provision reversal in Q4FY25 |
| Employee cost | ~-10% QoQ basis | down | Structural benefit flowing from plant-closure/VRS |
| Inventory | -13% YoY; **-28% over 2 yrs** | down | Availability up ~1,000 bps; complexity -30%; turns ~2.7 (target ~3) |
| Trade receivables | +65% YoY | up | Channel-mix driven (wholesale/franchise/B2B e-com credit); "base effect", no quality deterioration |
> One-offs hitting reported PBT (all flagged non-recurring/non-cash): (1) exceptional charge on closure of a manufacturing facility (structural cost-out, VRS); (2) ~INR22 cr (INR220m) Ind-AS FX revaluation of the brand-licensing liability at closing rate; (3) lower gain on lease/store closures — only INR3.6 cr vs INR8.4 cr LY (~INR4.8 cr non-cash delta); (4) base-quarter Q4FY25 carried a ~INR6 cr (INR60m) one-off provision reversal (COGS, vendor-reco), lifting the comparison base.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Growth:** No forward numbers given (policy). Momentum accelerating within Q4 (March > Jan); consumer sentiment "no tangible change" so far; conscious of inflation-driven unpredictability.
- **ZBM rollout:** 700 stores done by end-May'26 (contributing ~70% of COCO sales); target ~800-850 stores (~75-80% of network) by end of current quarter.
- **Franchise:** ~700 stores now → target close to/near 1,000 over next ~12 months.
- **Inventory:** ~70-75% of the journey done; push turns from ~2.7 toward ~3 without sacrificing availability.
- **Product:** Only ~10% of the product-reinvention investment has reached consumers; "massive upliftment" expected over next 12 months; sneaker proposition for younger consumers in active development.
- **Pricing:** Price hike NOT yet rolled out; will apply "judicious price elasticity" if RM inflation (~5-6% blended) persists.
- **Margins:** Underlying operating leverage to keep flowing through "ensuing periods"; gross-margin trajectory expected to improve as full-price mix builds.
order book & pipeline: - Not applicable (retailer, no order book). Network as the leading indicator: **2,000+ EBO stores** crossed (company milestone); ~700 omnichannel stores fulfilling online orders (~1,000 now serving online demand); MBO reach ~1,670 towns.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Retail (COCO, ~65% of business):** ~1,150 COCO stores; ZBM at 700 stores; 550 "pareto" larger stores = <50% of COCO count but >70% of COCO turnover. Volume-led DOS growth.
- **Franchise (FOFO) + SIS (~close to double digit %):** fastest-strategic-vector, double-digit growth, outright/bought-out model (Bata pays no lease rent — asset-light), accretive on per-pair EBIT despite optically lower gross margin %.
- **Multi-brand distribution / wholesale (MBO, ~10-12%):** ~1,670 towns; the <1,000-town drag is easing, signs of renewed growth momentum.
- **E-commerce (~12-13% of business; ~8-10% of revenue):** fastest-growing channel across B2B / B2C / bata.com. B2C ~half of e-com (~5-6%); within that bata.com ~14% (grew ~81% YoY, repeat sales ~doubled). Now accretive after 4-5 years of investment; doubles as a fast test-bed for products/promos.
- **Brand portfolio:** Hush Puppies (premium) = fastest-growing brand, ~18-20% of turnover, to be expanded disproportionately via own stores + franchise + SIS corners; HP and Power premium portfolios outpacing overall growth.
- **Channel split (FY):** COCO ~65%, non-COCO ~35% (franchise ~double digit, e-com ~8-10%, distribution ~10-12%).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Sneaker / athleisure proposition:** the single largest unlaunched lever to win younger consumers (big overlap with sneaker world); work in progress, to be unveiled "at the right moment."
- **Product reinvention funnel:** central design capability built around technology, comfort, style — "everyday footwear essential for every Indian family"; only ~10% manifested to consumers.
- **Premiumization:** Hush Puppies expansion + better-value premium products (not just price).
- **Value segment revival:** sub-INR1,000 (~35-40% of mix) has stopped declining after ~3 years of GST/RM-driven decline.
- **Omnichannel/quick-fulfilment:** leverage 2,000-store network as a forward stocking/quick-commerce-style fulfilment edge.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Reported gross margin masked by (a) franchise channel mix (lower GM% but EBIT-accretive) and (b) Q4FY25 base lifted by a ~INR6 cr provision reversal; underlying full-price sales growing ~2x company growth with lower markdowns → mgmt "reasonably hopeful" on GM trajectory.
- Operating leverage real: like-to-like PBT +11% (pre-Ind-AS profit +~16%), OCF +18%, employee cost ~-10% (plant-closure structural benefit).
- **RM inflation ~5-6% blended** (crude-linked EVA/PU; leather softer) — "waiting and watching", judged neutral for now, dynamic to crude.
- Marketing spend elevated (~1.5x), ~80-85% digital (digital marketing incl. performance), reflecting Ballerina Campaign + sneaker push; brand consideration at all-time high (66).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Asset-light tilt: franchise/SIS expansion needs little Bata capex (FOFO, no lease on Bata books); store expansion + ZBM rollout the main spend. Legacy manufacturing footprint being rationalised (plant closure this quarter — structural cost-out, not growth capex).
capital allocation:
- Structural cost-out via plant/factory closures + supplier consolidation (fewer, larger suppliers) to simplify the back end.
- Continued reinvestment in product design, marketing (~1.5x), and digital commerce. Working-capital release via inventory reduction funding the turnaround.
risks & watch-items:
- **Revenue stagnation:** ~4 years of flat top line; the re-acceleration is only 2 quarters old — execution risk on sustaining it.
- **Younger-consumer relevance:** "legacy brand" perception vs aspirational global/digital brands; the sneaker answer is still unlaunched.
- **RM/crude inflation** (~5-6%) + state minimum-wage hikes (Haryana, UP, Karnataka — structural/perennial) could pressure margins if not passed through; price hike not yet taken.
- **Gross margin optics** keep disappointing despite better mix (channel + base effects) — needs to actually show up.
- **Trade receivables +65% YoY** — mgmt says quality intact/base effect, but worth tracking days vs channel growth.
- **Reported vs adjusted gap:** -94% reported PBT, heavily adjusted — verify the one-offs are truly non-recurring.
management quality / tone: - CEO Gunjan Shah candid and consistent (same agenda tracked across quarters: inventory, ZBM, franchise, product, marketing), owns the multi-year stagnation, declines forward-looking numbers (disciplined). CFO Amit Aggarwal precise on the bridge from -94% reported to +11% like-for-like PBT and pre-Ind-AS +16%. Tone confident but measured; some deflection on the sneaker "answer" (teased, not disclosed). Engaged constructively with a pointed challenge on why the brand has under-delivered.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline -94% PBT is almost entirely cosmetic: a plant-closure VRS charge + a non-cash Ind-AS FX revaluation of the *brand-licensing liability* (a function of the global-parent royalty structure) + lower lease-closure gains + a flattered base quarter. Clean PBT +11%, pre-Ind-AS +16%, OCF +18% — the operating turn is real.
- Franchise (FOFO) is the quiet margin/return story: optically dilutes gross margin % but is EBIT-accretive per pair and asset-light (Bata bears no lease), so the mix shift improves ROCE even as reported GM% looks soft — a classic mix-misread for the market.
- Inventory is the engine: -28% over two years while availability +1,000 bps and complexity -30% has freed working capital and lifted full-price sales (~2x growth) — this funds the turnaround without heavy capex.
- The real swing factor is the unlaunched **sneaker proposition** aimed at the young/aspirational gap — that, plus the sub-INR1,000 value segment exiting a 3-year decline, are the two levers that could break the multi-year revenue plateau.
- bata.com +81% with repeat sales doubling makes e-com both a growth and a real-time product/promo test-bed — strategically more valuable than its ~14%-of-B2C revenue weight suggests.

Clean PBT +11%, pre-Ind-AS +16%, OCF +18% — the operating turn is real.
- Franchise (FOFO) is the quiet margin/return story: optically dilutes gross margin % but is EBIT-accretive per pair and asset-light (Bata bears no lease), so the mix shift improves ROCE even as reported GM% looks soft — a classic mix-misread for the market.
- Inventory is the engine: -28% over two years while availability +1,000 bps and complexity -30% has freed working capital and lifted full-price sales (~2x growth) — this funds the turnaround without heavy capex.
- The real swing factor is the unlaunched **sneaker proposition** aimed at the young/aspirational gap — that, plus the sub-INR1,000 value segment exiting a 3-year decline, are the two levers that could break the multi-year revenue plateau.
- bata.com +81% with repeat sales doubling makes e-com both a growth and a real-time product/promo test-bed — strategically more valuable than its ~14%-of-B2C revenue weight suggests.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

hero.oneLiner: Bata delivered a second consecutive quarter of accelerating, volume-backed ~5%+ value growth with broad-based gains across channels and categories, while a structural turnaround (zero-based merchandising at 700 stores, inventory down 28% over two years, franchise/SIS expansion, the 2,000-store EBO milestone) is finally translating into ~11% like-for-like PBT growth and +18% operating cash flow. Reported PBT collapsed ~94% purely on non-recurring/non-cash items (a manufacturing-plant closure/VRS charge, a ~INR22 cr Ind-AS FX revaluation of the brand-licensing liability, and lower lease-closure gains), and the multi-year revenue stagnation is being attacked through product reinvention (only ~10% of which has reached consumers), a forthcoming sneaker proposition for younger buyers, and a stabilising sub-INR1,000 value segment.
